title: A tangent you can edit
problem: Find the tangent line to f(x)=x^2+2x at x=1.
source_note: Original example. Edit this JSON to create another authored walkthrough; each step contains one equation and its explanation.

steps.title: Start with the function
steps.why: The graph shows the original curve. We want the line touching it at x=1.
steps.narration: We want a tangent to this curve at x equals one.

steps.title: Differentiate both terms
steps.why: The power rule differentiates x squared; the derivative of 2x is 2.
steps.narration: Differentiate term by term to obtain two x plus two.

steps.title: Evaluate the slope
steps.why: A derivative evaluated at the base point gives the tangent slope.
steps.narration: At x equals one the slope is four.

steps.title: Find the point
steps.why: The tangent passes through the original curve at x=1.
steps.narration: The height of the curve at one is three.

steps.title: Use point-slope form
steps.why: Insert slope 4 and point (1,3). This line has the same local slope as the curve.
steps.narration: The tangent is y minus three equals four times x minus one.

steps.title: Simplify the line
steps.why: Distribute 4, then add 3 to both sides.
steps.narration: Distributing and collecting constants gives y equals four x minus one.
